evidence.title: EF-210: why 20 minutes?
evidence.claim: In 2001, Gastaldi requested the 20-minute wait, possibly to allow bubbles to escape, though the exact reason was undocumented in 2009.
evidence.quote: Gastaldi wanted it in 2001. I don't know why. Maybe to let the bubbles out?

evidence.title: LABORATORY TEST REPORT LT-2004-061
evidence.claim: In 2004, air entrained by micro-silica during filler addition caused pinholes in EF-210, supporting the theory that air release is a known issue.
evidence.quote: air is entrained by the micro-silica during filler addition and released during curing

evidence.title: CUSTOMER CLAIM CL-2004-003
evidence.claim: In 2004, customer Logistica Fontanili reported pinholes and craters on a floor coated with EF-210, requiring a full recoating.
evidence.quote: Complaint: pinholes and craters across the floor; recoating required.

evidence.title: Supplier qualification SQ-2012-007 - Kessler-Ondra Harze GmbH, KO-Epox 410 LC
evidence.claim: In 2012, the resin ALTAREP E-19 was replaced by KO-Epox 410 LC for EF-210 Part A.
evidence.quote: approved; replaces ALTAREP E-19 from May 2012

evidence.title: Minutes - EF-210 cycle time review, 9 February 2021
evidence.claim: In 2021, the use of micro-silica was maintained to ensure sag resistance, confirming the continued presence of the material that causes air entrainment.
evidence.quote: Rejected: micro-silica is needed for sag resistance on ramps and vertical surfaces (customer specification). Vacuum stays.

verdict.process_name: EF-210 epoxy floor coating, Part A
verdict.instruction: Wait 20 min after the diluent addition before taking the viscosity sample.
verdict.reason: The step was introduced by Gastaldi in 2001 (E3). While the exact reason was undocumented, air entrainment from micro-silica causing pinholes was confirmed in 2004 (E4, E5). Micro-silica remains a required component for sag resistance as of 2021 (E7), meaning the hazard of air entrainment persists.

chain.claim: Micro-silica causes air entrainment leading to pinholes in EF-210
Micro-silica is still used in the product for sag resistance

dependencies.name: micro-silica causing air entrainment

counter_evidence.claim: The exact reason for the wait was unknown in 2009
counter_evidence.resolution: Subsequent lab reports (E4) and claims (E5) linked the product's air issues to the filler used.
